5. In the suit, plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and filed the documents marked as exhibits 1-6. Defendants also examined 4 witnesses and filed documents as exhibits Ka to Kha. Learned Judge found the defendants case totally not sustainable in law and decreed the suit to the tune of Taka 1,50,000,00 which in the incidental value of the policy. 

 6. Mr. Md Oziullah, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant of FA No.472 of 2012, submits that as per section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 learned Judge ought to award interest over the decretal amount. Learned Advocate further submits that his client did not challenge the judgment but since according to law plaintiff entitled to interest as per section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 learned Judge ought to decree the suit with interest. 

 12. We at first take up the case of Rupali Insurance Company i.e. First Appeal No. 385 of 2012 and Appeal From Original Decree No. 472 of 2012 of the plaintiff entirely rests on the decision of this appeal. 

 19. The decree passed by the learned Judge is modified to the time of Taka 1,12,08.000 deducting subrogated amount at Taka 14,10,000 Taka 97,98,000. Upon which as per section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 i.e. if there be any decree passed, Court shall impose pendentillite interest at the rate of five percent (5%) higher than the prevailing bank rate. 

 20. Section 47B (2) provides that interest under sub-section (1) shall be payable for the period during which the failure continues and shall be calculated at monthly rates at the rate of five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate. Decree passed by the learned Judge is modified to the tune of Taka 97,98,000 with interest shall be paid monthly at the rate of five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate from the date of receipt of this order. 

 21. In the result, First Appeal No. 472 of 2012 is allowed in part with modification of decree as aforesaid and First Appeal No.385 of 2012 is dismissed.
